definition: In image processing, ridge detection is the attempt, via software, to locate ridges in an image, defined as curves whose points are local maxima of the function, akin to geographical ridges.
details: For a function of N variables, its ridges are a set of curves whose points are local maxima in N − 1 dimensions. In this respect, the notion of ridge points extends the concept of a local maximum. Correspondingly, the notion of valleys for a function can be defined by replacing the condition of a local maximum with the condition of a local minimum. The union of ridge sets and valley sets, together with a related set of points called the connector set, form a connected set of curves that partition, intersect, or meet at the critical points of the function. This union of sets together is called the function's relative critical set. Ridge sets, valley sets, and relative critical sets represent important geometric information intrinsic to a function. In a way, they provide a compact representation of important features of the function, but the extent to which they can be used to determine global features of the function is an open question. The primary motivation for the creation of ridge detection and valley detection procedures has come from image analysis and computer vision and is to capture the interior of elongated objects in the image domain. explainer.lead: Ridge detection is the software-based attempt to locate ridges in an image, defined as curves whose points are local maxima of the function, akin to geographical ridges. It matters because it extends the idea of a local maximum from points to curves.

tiers.eli5: Imagine finding the crest lines of a mountain range on a map: ridge detection draws those crest lines through an image instead of just marking the single highest peak.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use ridge detection to extract curvilinear structures from images, working with the local-maximum condition across dimensions. A pitfall is that the definition depends on dimensionality, since a ridge is a local maximum in N − 1 dimensions rather than in all N.
tiers.paperLevel: For a function of N variables, its ridges are a set of curves whose points are local maxima in N − 1 dimensions; valleys are defined by replacing local maximum with local minimum, and ridges, valleys and a connector set form connected curves that partition the domain.

explainer.example: For a function of two variables, a ridge is a curve along which each point is a local maximum in the one remaining dimension, like a line of peaks across a surface.
